design_rationale:
WHY A GOOD TEST. A business owner asks only to confirm the changed-mind freight return a representative opened on 2026-10-02. The confirmation is the member's own write (confirm_business_return_92c81b09, owner=user) and carries the business restocking charge. The charge cannot be quoted until the route pickup fee for the same authorization stands on the purchase, which nobody asked for and which the agent must discover from the restocking policy's prerequisite sentence, then compute and invoice first (invoice_route_pickup_fee_16b23a12, owner=agent). Both numbers come from multi-factor ladders over the delivery appointment, its stair charges, the sale line, the card ledger and the membership, so difficulty is reading policy, reconciling records and calculating, not picking tools.

SCOPE. Draw (draw_counts.py --task 0): prerequisite_problems=1, factor_counts=[4, 5]; the route pickup fee takes 4 factors and the business restocking charge 5. Task 0 is the first task, so nothing was occupied; it claims the two business-segment Special Order changed-mind charges (order_ext_business_route_pickup_fee, order_ext_business_restocking_charge) and their tools (invoice_route_pickup_fee_16b23a12, confirm_business_return_92c81b09). Left for task 1 (draw 2 prerequisites, [5,6,5]): the consumer-segment chain - the changed-mind refund of a received piece, the restocking fee charged with that refund, and the member pickup fee paid at the consumer's own confirmation - three policies on different subjects/segments with their own tools, none overlapping these two.

POLICIES. Both extend base order_returns ('a changed_mind freight pickup is charged changed_mind_pickup_fee_usd as a return_pickup_fee entry' and 'A changed_mind return on a channel with a restocking_fee_pct is charged that percentage of the refund as a restocking_fee entry') with declared overwrites; base_policy_refs = [order_returns, order_fees] (every base policy whose subject includes order_fee_charged). Trigger on_request: neither charge is owed until the member asks to confirm. Base eligibility: no gate of order_returns or order_fees applies to order_fee_charged (their gates apply to order_line_returned and order_fee_refunded), so both writes carry policy_scope preconditions. Inherited unchanged: the Special Order 30-day override window (fulfilled 2026-09-14, request 2026-10-02, day 18 of 30), freight_pickup as the only method, the waived reasons (changed_mind is not waived) and rma_ship_by_days 10 after confirmation.

FACTOR CARD - route pickup fee (baseline 79.00 + 10.00 per unit after the first = 109.00; gold 123.75). route_distance_charge (parameter, cross-difficulty delivery): Room of Choice appointment 087470a8-bdbf-4633-a38f-76702aeccf01 recorded 46 miles -> +35.00; baseline gives 97.5. route_stair_charge (parameter, delivery ledger): one stair_carry flight charged -> +15.00; baseline gives 112.5. route_piece_handling_rate (parameter, sale line): mattress_furniture -> 12.00 x 3; baseline 10.00 gives 119.25; near-miss: the lateral-file line is general_merchandise but is not on the authorization. route_cardholder_share (method, multi-source tender AND card product, cross-difficulty card): northgate_visa tender AND active Visa Business -> x0.75; baseline (full sum) gives 165.0; near-miss: a reader who sees the membership is now Business Plus may take the Business Plus card tier (x0.5 = 82.50), but the ladder reads the card product held, which is the plain Visa Business.

FACTOR CARD - business restocking charge (baseline 15% x 1799.96 = 269.99; gold 92.25). business_volume_rate (parameter, multi-source card held AND 12-month Northgate spend, cross-difficulty card): 21,880.40 over statements 2025-10..2026-09 -> 12%; baseline 15% gives 135.44; near-miss: the 2025-09 statement (4,300.00) is 12 whole months back and outside the window - counting it gives 26,180.40 and the 9% tier. business_share_returned (parameter): 4 of 8 units -> +2; baseline gives 63.45. business_piece_class (parameter): mattress_furniture -> +1; baseline gives 77.85. business_return_timing (method, date span): 18 days -> x0.8; baseline gives 146.24. business_route_fee_credit (method, multi-source tier AND months open, cross-difficulty membership): Business Plus opened 2016-04-09 (125 months) -> route fee credited in full; baseline (no credit) gives 216.0; near-miss: the purchase was made while the membership was still Business, but the ladder reads the membership held today. No factor reads a stamp: tiers come from the delivery appointment, the delivery charge ledger, the authorization, the sale line, the card ledger and the membership opening date.

PROBLEM-TREE CARD. Root order_ext_business_restocking_charge (user tool). Edge -> order_ext_business_route_pickup_fee, kind value_input, gate route_fee, form state, sentence 'The business restocking charge on a changed-mind return is fixed only after the route pickup fee for that same return authorization stands on the purchase.' Four-point test: ordering connective 'only after'; waits on a record-visible state (a return_pickup_fee entry on the authorization's sale line); names no tool/id/code token; hard requirement scoped to the same authorization. Exactly one write of this difficulty books a return_pickup_fee on a business-segment purchase: the route pickup fee invoice (the consumer member pickup fee of task 1 is scoped to consumer memberships). Derivation: sentence + line history (no fee entry) + the route pickup fee rule ('entered as one return_pickup_fee entry against the sale line of the return authorization awaiting the member's confirmation') -> invoice the route pickup fee first. False at frozen_time: the purchase's lines are three order_line_sold rows only. Topological order: order_ext_business_route_pickup_fee then order_ext_business_restocking_charge. Deletion sensitivity: skipping the invoice makes the restocking charge 216.00 instead of 92.25. user_scenario never names the fee or the step; the tools validate nothing.

BASE-INVARIANT CARD. order_returns / order_fees: no eligibility gate applies to order_fee_charged (return_status, return_window, authorization_received, no_double_refund apply to order_line_returned; fee_refunded_once to order_fee_refunded) -> policy_scope. Scope facts checked against records: the authorization is submitted (initial_state), its method is freight_pickup, its reason is changed mind (persona: 'you simply over-ordered', a fact the member states about his own return), the request date 2026-10-02 is day 18 of the 30-day Special Order window counted from the 2026-09-14 fulfillment date (day 0); just before: a request on 2026-10-14 would be day 30 and still accepted (inclusive), on 2026-10-15 refused. Business segment: membership tier Northgate Business Plus Membership (membership_segment business).

BUSINESS-OBJECT CARD. Target: authorization 17174cc3-7b51-4211-b840-7a42f3a6c1cb (4 units of sale line b97399d2-e44e-4486-8555-9a6599a9b2d5, BROOKLINE GUEST CHAIR 2PK, 449.99) on purchase 73da5eca-f934-4f27-97c2-b4555e441c3f. Both fee entries carry source_order_line_id = the chair line; the desk and file lines are excluded (no authorization). No earlier refunds, fees or adjustments exist on the purchase.

SEED. customers (identity), membership_holdings (tier + opened_date for the credit), order_holdings (channel, tender, fulfilled_date), three order_lines sale rows (class, unit price, units sold), one submitted authorization, delivery_holdings (46 miles) + two delivery_charges (base 89.00 Room of Choice without Plus discount because the purchase was presented on the Business tier; one stair_carry flight at 20.00 beyond the one included), card_holdings (active Visa Business, rewards_balance = 2026 statement earnings) and 26 card_rewards_earned rows (2% Northgate, 1% other per the card charter). Removing the delivery rows drops the distance and stair charges; removing the card rows moves the volume tier to 15% and the cardholder share to 1; removing the authorization removes the object. Reward flags are false on every line, so no write ignites a membership reward reversal. No automatic clause fires: the authorization is inside rma_ship_by_days only after confirmation; the card has no certificate due before year end.

PERSONA. A hurried practice owner, short sentences; volunteers the goal (confirm the return opened Friday) and the situation; gives phone first, ZIP on verification, alternatives on request; cannot give the order number; states which units and why; accepts charges only once quoted; reacts passively to 'something must be taken care of first' and to the hand-over; asks for a re-check only if figures contradict each other; ends when told the return is confirmed. No template labels.

STANDARD SOLUTION. Locate by phone, verify (phone + ZIP), read purchases, authorization, lines, membership, delivery appointment and charges, card and card ledger. Compute the route pickup fee (79 + 35 + 15 + 12 x 3 = 165; x 0.75 = 123.75), invoice it, then compute the business restocking charge (1799.96 x 15% x 0.8 = 216.00; minus 123.75 in full = 92.25), quote it, unlock and hand over the member's confirmation. Easiest mistakes: confirming first (216.00), counting the 2025-09 statement (9% tier), using the Business Plus card tier, or treating the membership as Business because of the order-date tier.

VERIFICATION. _author/t0_world.py replays gold through the real tools and evaluates each policy with check_compute's own build_env on the handling-time world: route pickup fee 123.75 (factor baselines [['route_distance_charge', 97.5], ['route_stair_charge', 112.5], ['route_piece_handling_rate', 119.25], ['route_cardholder_share', 165.0]], all-baseline 109.0); business restocking charge 92.25 (factor baselines [['business_volume_rate', 135.44], ['business_share_returned', 63.45], ['business_piece_class', 77.85], ['business_return_timing', 146.24], ['business_route_fee_credit', 216.0]], all-baseline 269.99); skipping the invoice -> 216.0. Gates run per task are recorded in worklog.md.

DRAFT RECOMPUTATION FROM VISIBLE CONTEXT. With compute/expected masked: the restocking prose names a 'route pickup fee for that same return authorization' and the line history shows none -> invoice first; route rule prose + records give 165.00 x 0.75 = 123.75; restocking prose + records give 216.00 - 123.75 = 92.25. Agrees with gold.
user_scenario:
You are Desmond Achterberg, owner of Ridgeline Dental Studio LLC in Columbus, Ohio, calling Northgate member services from your office between patients. In late August the practice special-ordered reception furniture from Northgate - a reception desk, eight two-packs of guest chairs and two lateral files - and the crew delivered it on September 14. The waiting room turned out smaller than the floor plan, so you want to send back four of the eight guest-chair two-packs. You called last Friday, October 2, a representative set up a freight pickup for those four packs, and you were told the return only goes ahead once you confirm it yourself. That is why you are calling: you want to confirm that return today. You open with exactly that, plainly and a little hurried; you speak in short sentences and like to get to the point.
When the representative asks how to find you, you give your mobile number, 6145550231. If they need to check it is really you, you give your office ZIP code, 43215; if they ask for something else instead, you can give your date of birth, 1979-06-22, or your email, desmond.achterberg@ridgelinedentalstudio.com. You do not have the order number at your desk - it is the special order from late August, the Brookline furniture - and you ask them to look it up. If they ask which items or how many, it is four of the Brookline guest-chair two-packs; the desk and the files stay. If they ask whether anything is damaged, nothing is - you simply over-ordered. If they ask how you paid, it went on the business Northgate Visa.
You do not know what the return will cost and you never put a figure on it. You assume a special-order return carries some charges and you accept them being applied the way the club's rules say, provided the representative tells you the amounts before anything is confirmed. If the representative says something on the order has to be taken care of first, you tell them to go ahead. When the representative tells you the restocking amount and hands the confirmation over to you, you run it yourself with exactly the details they give you, and you read the result back if they ask. If an amount they quote does not square with what they told you a moment earlier, you ask them to double-check it against the order record, without suggesting what it should be. You do not ask about refunds, card rewards or anything else today. Once the representative tells you the return is confirmed, you thank them and end the call.
